sites.name: Danone - Mount Crawford VA
sites.dossierExcerpt:
- Name: Danone - Mount Crawford VA
- Type: Multi-category beverage plant (refrigerated) — Silk, International Delight, SToK, So Delicious, Horizon, Dunkin'
- Address: 6364 South Valley Pike, Mount Crawford, VA 22841
- Resolved center: 38.36880, -78.93980

fieldNotes.truckGate: Both road accesses off South Valley Pike are wide open driveways with no barrier arm, sliding gate, or checkpoint pinch-point. Street View at the east main entry (38.3657,-78.9376) shows an open driveway with only directional signage ('ALL LIQUID AND OKARA RECEIVING / ALL COLD & DRY STORAGE RECEIVING OFF #1'), confirming a self-routed ungated site.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth visible at any entrance; drivers self-route via posted signs.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus: main 640k sq ft refrigerated plant, a separate west annex/DC building with its own docks and trailer rows, a wastewater treatment area, plus an extensive tank/silo farm.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Hundreds of trailers parked in long rows along the west and north perimeter of the main building and around the annex; clearly a 50+ drop operation.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Long dock apron on the west face of the main building with many trailers backed in (~40-50 doors), plus additional dock banks on the annex and the liquid-receiving area; total estimated 60, banded 50+.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Posted signage directs liquid/okara receiving and cold/dry receiving to different entrances/dock areas; receiving and shipping run from physically distinct dock clusters.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified in overhead imagery; possible but not confirmed - listed uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide entrance aprons and large internal yard with ample unused paved width.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Two separate road accesses off South Valley Pike (east main entry and a central/west drive), functioning as distinct in/out points.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur runs into the property.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved internal yard between the trailer rows and the dock doors provides ample interior staging.

sites.name: Danone - Dallas TX
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster coordinates (32.705103, -96.920756, ROOFTOP, 163 m move) landed directly
on a large industrial building with extensive rooftop process equipment
(refrigeration units, vertical tanks, pipe racks) consistent with a refrigerated
beverage plant. Satellite at z16-z20 confirmed a two-building campus fronting Dan
Morton Drive. The Danone monument sign is visible in Street View at the west
entrance. The 357,000 sq ft figure (main) plus 252,000 sq ft (toppers) matches the
two distinct buildings. Locked center on the main complex.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Both road entrances off Dan Morton Drive are wide, open driveways with no barrier arm or sliding gate. Street View (Jan 2025) shows a tractor freely turning into the west driveway with no checkpoint pinch-point. Perimeter is fenced but road access is uncontrolled.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at either entrance in Street View or satellite imagery. Web research confirms drivers 'check in at the office' for door assignment - check-in is at the building, not a gate booth.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because there is no controlled truck gate at all (remoteGs requires a gate).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of two large buildings: 357,000 sq ft main plant (west/center) and 252,000 sq ft toppers building (east), separated by an internal driveway.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock banks on the north faces of both the main building and the east toppers building - two physically distinct dock clusters.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer drop lot on the west side of the property with ~30+ trailers parked in marked rows, separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: Estimate ~60 across both north dock faces; partly obscured by parked trailers in imagery - low confidence, banded 50+.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide gate aprons at both entrances with ample unused paved width for an express bypass lane.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved yard areas inside the property between road and dock faces give trucks room to queue/stage.

sites.name: Danone - DuBois PA
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster flagged a 3,159 m geocode move, so location was verified carefully.
Satellite at z17 around the roster point (41.105801, -78.731049) showed a large
industrial building set in forested countryside — consistent with the only Danone
NA plant-based yogurt plant. Street View (Jun 2025) along Oklahoma-Salem Road
confirmed a Danone-branded plant with the company sign and US/PA flags at the
green-fronted office. The 24-acre / 189,158 sq ft figures from web research match
the compact two-building complex. Coordinates confirmed correct.

fieldNotes.truckGate: The plant driveway off Oklahoma-Salem Road is a paved open driveway with directional pavement arrows but no barrier arm or sliding gate at the road. A decorative metal fence with stone pillars runs along the road frontage, but the driveway entrance itself is uncontrolled (Street View Jun 2025).
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth visible at the driveway entrance or the internal Y-fork in Street View or satellite. A small orange-roofed structure near the building SE corner is a pump/utility house, not a gate booth.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False - no controlled truck gate exists.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: buildingCount=2 (main plant plus the blue-roofed building to the south), but they read as one integrated plant complex on one property, so multipleFacilities (campus) is false.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Compact 189,158 sq ft plant; dock face partly under a blue sawtooth canopy on the west side. Estimate ~14 doors - low confidence due to snow-tinted, moderate-resolution imagery.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Only ~3-4 trailers visible in an informal staging area NE of the building; no marked drop-yard stalls. Banded 0-10, low confidence.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural - the plant sits in forested countryside outside DuBois, PA, surrounded by woods with only scattered rural homes nearby.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Rural forested setting; the town of DuBois is a few km away so coverage is likely adequate but not certain - flagged as medium confidence.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The driveway from the road to the dock area is long and curving with ample room for a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large open paved/graded yard areas inside the property give trucks room to stage before the docks.

sites.name: Danone - Springfield OR
sites.dossierExcerpt:
Roster coordinates (44.065549, -123.04481, ROOFTOP, 25 m move) landed inside a
multi-tenant industrial park between Highway 126 and a residential neighborhood.
The park has several similar warehouse buildings, so the exact plant was confirmed
by Street View: a building carries a clear "Danone North America" logo by its
office entrance (Street View Jul 2024). Web research confirms the legacy Turtle
Mountain / So Delicious plant, ~2.5-acre footprint, ~150 employees. Coordinates
confirmed; locked center on the Danone-branded building cluster.

fieldNotes.truckGate: A sliding chain-link gate spans the truck/process drive aisle between the plant buildings (visible in Street View Jul 2024). The gate encloses the production yard with its tanks and reefer trailers. It is a controlled pinch-point across the truck lane = truckGate true.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth - the gate is a plain sliding chain-link gate with no booth structure beside it. Driver check-in is at the building office (the Danone-branded entrance).
fieldNotes.remoteGs: True - there is a controlled gate but no guard shack, implying keypad/call-box/buzz-in check-in.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: The Danone operation occupies ~3 connected/adjacent buildings (~2.5 acres total) within a larger multi-tenant industrial park. It reads as one small integrated plant, not a multi-building campus, so multipleFacilities is false. Note other tenants in the park (e.g. a CrossFit gym) are unrelated.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: The truck yard between buildings is very tight - a confined courtyard-style yard. A truck queue would quickly choke the shared park drive aisle, so backup-sensitive.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Short, confined approach - room for only 1-2 trucks between the gate and the dock.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Small frozen-dessert plant; only a handful of dock doors visible (estimate ~8). Low confidence - dock face is partly obscured by parked reefer trailers and a covered conveyor structure.
fieldNotes.dropArea: No dedicated marked trailer drop stalls; trailers seen are backed in at docks or staged transiently in the tight yard.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban - the plant sits within the dense industrial/residential fabric of Springfield, OR, beside Highway 126.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Single shared gate/drive serves both entry and exit; lane count not separately determinable - flagged uncertain.

sites.name: Danone - Fort Worth TX
sites.dossierExcerpt:
Roster coordinates (32.741022, -97.339329, ROOFTOP, 121 m move) landed on a large
multi-building industrial complex in Fort Worth's Near Southside district, directly
adjacent to Interstate 30. Web research confirms the historic Dannon Fort Worth
plant: founded 1925, 10.9-acre site, ~210 employees, producing Danimals, Activia
and YoCrunch. Street View confirms a "Shipping & Receiving" sign at the truck gate.
Coordinates confirmed correct.

fieldNotes.truckGate: A sliding chain-link gate spans the truck driveway off the west street, with a 'Shipping & Receiving' directional sign at the entrance (Street View Jan 2025). Clear controlled truck gate.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth - no small windowed structure beside the gate in Street View or satellite. The 'Shipping & Receiving' sign directs drivers; check-in is at the building.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: True - a controlled gate exists with no guard shack, implying call-box/intercom/app check-in.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Dense urban site with the truck gate opening directly onto a narrow city street and little stacking room - a truck queue would spill onto the public street. Backup-sensitive.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Tight urban site; the gate-to-dock approach holds only 1-2 trucks.
fieldNotes.dropYard: A fenced trailer/equipment yard on the west side holds parked trailers (XTRA Lease and other rental reefers) and equipment laydown, separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Historic dense plant (founded 1925, 10.9 acres); dock doors spread across building faces are partly obscured by parked trailers and process structures. Estimate ~18, banded 10-25 - moderate confidence.
fieldNotes.railServed: Mainline railroad tracks run parallel to the plant's north edge beneath the I-30 overpass, but no spur turns into the property - not rail-served.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: One large contiguous multi-section plant building, not a multi-building campus.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban - the plant sits in Fort Worth's dense Near Southside district, adjacent to I-30, surrounded by city streets and commercial blocks.

sites.name: Danone - Bridgeton NJ
sites.dossierExcerpt:
Roster coordinates (39.446174, -75.213811, ROOFTOP, 330 m move) landed on a large
industrial building fronting Rosenhayn Avenue. Web research confirms the Danone
Bridgeton plant: 185,000 sq ft, operating since 2001, ~120 employees, producing
Silk plant-based beverages. Street View (Dec 2025) shows a "DANONE" monument sign
and US flags at the front of the building. (Note: a separate large distribution
warehouse with many trailers sits to the NW — that is a different facility, not
Danone.) Coordinates confirmed correct.

fieldNotes.truckGate: The main driveway off Rosenhayn Avenue is a wide open driveway with no barrier arm or sliding gate at the road. There are pavement stop/lane markings partway down the drive but no controlled checkpoint structure. The driveway feeds a perimeter loop road to the docks.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth at the driveway or anywhere on the perimeter. A Danone monument sign and flags stand at the front; the small structures by the south dock are tank/silo pads (process equipment), not gate booths.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False - there is no controlled truck gate at all.
fieldNotes.dropYard: A dedicated trailer drop yard on the SE side of the property holds ~12 trailers parked in angled marked stalls, separate from the active dock face.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: A large paved maneuvering/staging area sits inside the property between the perimeter road and the south dock face.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The driveway plus the perimeter loop road to the docks is long, with ample room for a 3+ truck queue.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dock face along the building's south side with trailers backed in; estimate ~22 doors, banded 10-25 - moderate confidence due to trailer occlusion.
fieldNotes.dropArea: ~12 trailers in marked drop stalls in the SE drop yard, banded 10-25.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural - the plant sits on the edge of Bridgeton, NJ (a small South Jersey city) with farmland, woods, and scattered houses around it; not dense metro fabric.
fieldNotes.operationalNote: Closure announced - Danone plans to shut this plant Aug 2, 2026 with 114 layoffs, relocating Silk production to Mount Crawford VA, Dallas TX, and Jacksonville FL. Still operating as of the May 2026 audit date; imagery (satellite + Dec 2025 Street View) shows active trailers and dock use.
